day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Montreal — Flight AC lands at 13:00, so no morning activities scheduled. Use this time to rest on the plane.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing and collecting luggage, take the 747 STM airport express bus (~$11 CAD) to downtown, then connect to Old Montreal. Check into your accommodation, freshen up, and take a relaxed self-guided walk through the cobblestone streets of Old Montreal to get your bearings — explore Place Jacques-Cartier, the waterfront Vieux-Port, and admire the Notre-Dame Basilica exterior for free.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Montreal Jazz Festival (Festival International de Jazz) at the Quartier des Spectacles, just a short Metro or bus ride from Old Montreal. Enjoy the free outdoor stages featuring world-class jazz, blues, and world music performances. Soak in the festive atmosphere with thousands of locals.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a quick bite at the airport.
meals.lunch: Pick up a budget-friendly poutine or smoked meat sandwich from a grab-and-go spot near Old Montreal after check-in — try Chez Claudette or a nearby dépanneur snack (~$10–14 CAD).
meals.dinner: Grab a crepe or a hot dog québécois from one of the many affordable food stands and food trucks set up around the Jazz Festival grounds at Quartier des Spectacles (~$8–12 CAD). Pair with a local Boréale beer from a festival vendor.

day_by_day.notes: The 747 STM bus is the most budget-friendly airport transfer (~$11 CAD, covers 24-hour transit pass). Jazz Festival free outdoor concerts run nightly — no ticket needed for the main outdoor stages. Wear comfortable walking shoes for cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour — Take the Metro (Orange Line) north to Jean-Talon station. Spend the morning exploring one of North America's largest open-air markets. Sample Quebec cheeses, maple products, fresh fruits, artisan breads, and local charcuterie. Many vendors offer free tastings. Stock up on affordable picnic supplies like fresh produce, local cheese, and baguettes for later.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Plateau-Mont-Royal neighbourhood and explore Avenue du Mont-Royal and Saint-Denis Street on foot. Browse eclectic boutiques and murals, then head to Parc La Fontaine for a relaxing picnic with your Jean-Talon Market finds. Enjoy the park's beautiful lake and gardens — a favourite local hangout.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Montreal Jazz Festival at Quartier des Spectacles for another evening of free outdoor concerts. Tonight, explore the side streets around Saint-Denis and Ontario for live music spilling out of small bars and terrasses.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh croissant and café au lait from a local boulangerie near your Old Montreal accommodation (~$5–7 CAD). Try Olive + Gourmando if open, or a nearby corner bakery.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Parc La Fontaine using fresh market finds from Jean-Talon — cheese, bread, fruit, and charcuterie purchased for ~$10–14 CAD total.
meals.dinner: Try a classic Quebec meal at a budget-friendly BYOB (apportez votre vin) restaurant on Saint-Denis Street — look for a table d'hôte (set menu) deal, often $18–25 CAD for a full meal. Try La Banquise for a legendary poutine dinner (~$14–18 CAD) — open 24 hours and a Montreal institution.

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is best visited early morning (9–11 AM) for the freshest selection and fewest crowds. The Metro day pass (~$11 CAD) is great value if you plan multiple trips. BYOB restaurants are a uniquely Montreal budget-friendly dining tradition — grab a bottle of wine from a SAQ or dépanneur beforehand.

day_by_day.morning: Old Montreal Street Food & History Walk — Start the morning with a self-guided (free) or budget walking tour of Old Montreal's historic streets. Visit Rue Saint-Paul for local bakeries and pastry shops. Stop at a traditional boulangerie for a pain au chocolat, then explore the Bonsecours Market building (free to enter) and the historic waterfront. Hunt for maple taffy samples and sugar shack treats at specialty shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Just for Laughs Festival Street Performances — The Just for Laughs (Just pour rire) Festival runs in mid-July. Head to Saint-Denis Street and the Latin Quarter to catch free outdoor comedy performances, street acts, clowns, and surprise parades. The street programming is entirely free and runs throughout the afternoon into the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Continue enjoying the Just for Laughs Festival street atmosphere as it peaks in the evening. Grab street food from vendors along the festival route, then wind down with a stroll back through Old Montreal along the illuminated waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Freshly baked bagel (Montreal-style, wood-fired) from a local spot — grab a half-dozen from Fairmount Bagel or St-Viateur Bagel (both ~$1 CAD per bagel) with cream cheese (~$6–8 total). Worth the short trip to the Plateau.
meals.lunch: Grab a budget street food lunch near the Just for Laughs festival zone — shawarma wraps on Saint-Denis are excellent value (~$9–12 CAD). Try a local Lebanese or Middle Eastern spot, which are plentiful and affordable in the area.
meals.dinner: Enjoy a casual dinner at a terrasse (outdoor patio) restaurant near Old Montreal or the waterfront. Try moules-frites (mussels and fries) at a brasserie — look for early-bird or happy hour specials (~$18–22 CAD). Alternatively, grab a smoked meat sandwich at a deli-style spot (~$12–15 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: Just for Laughs street performances are 100% free — no tickets required. Check the festival app or website for the daily parade schedule so you don't miss it. Friday evenings are especially lively. Wear sunscreen — the warm summer weather (25°C) means you'll be outside most of the day.

day_by_day.morning: Hike or walk up Mont Royal — Take Bus 11 from Mont-Royal Metro station to the top of the mountain (included in transit fare). Enjoy panoramic views of the entire city from the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout. Walk through the forested trails, spot local wildlife, and visit Beaver Lake (Lac aux Castors). This is a beloved free activity that every Montrealer cherishes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend Mont Royal and explore the Mile End neighbourhood — one of Montreal's hippest and most culturally rich areas. Wander Bernard Avenue and Laurier Street, admire street art and murals, and pop into independent record shops and boutiques. Visit the famous Alley (Ruelle Verte) murals. End the afternoon with one final loop through the Quartier des Spectacles to soak up any remaining festival energy from both Jazz Fest and Just for Laughs.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your final evening back in Old Montreal for a farewell walk along the Vieux-Port waterfront as the sun sets over the St. Lawrence River. Enjoy the golden hour views, then treat yourself to a slightly indulgent but still budget-friendly farewell dinner before wrapping up your Montreal adventure.

meals.breakfast: Pick up a hearty breakfast sandwich or avocado toast from a café in Old Montreal before heading to Mont Royal (~$8–10 CAD). Alternatively, grab pastries and coffee from a local dépanneur to eat at the mountain summit.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic or grab a sandwich from a Mile End café to enjoy in the neighbourhood (~$10–13 CAD). Try a smoked meat sandwich from a local deli or a falafel wrap from a Mile End Middle Eastern spot.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a beloved Old Montreal restaurant — treat yourself to a Quebec-inspired meal. Try a tourtière (meat pie) or a Quebecois tasting plate at a mid-range spot where you can eat well for ~$22–28 CAD. Look for happy hour specials or a table d'hôte. End with a traditional sugar pie (tarte au sucre) for dessert (~$5 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: Mont Royal is free to access and one of the best budget activities in the city. Bring water and sunscreen. Saturday markets and street festivals are especially lively — keep an eye out for impromptu drum circles at Mont Royal (a beloved Montreal tradition, especially Sunday afternoons). Check transit schedules if departing Montreal on this day or the next morning.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport before landing.

meals.dinner: Dine at Taverne Gaspar on Rue de la Commune in Old Montreal — a mid-range brasserie with local Québécois dishes, craft beers, and a lively terrace perfect for a first night out (~$35–50 CAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight lands at 13:00, allow roughly 1.5–2 hours for baggage, customs, and transit to the hotel before beginning the afternoon walk. The Jazz Festival runs from late June through mid-July — confirm the exact schedule and free stage lineup on the official festival website before attending. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Take the Metro (Orange Line) north to Jean-Talon Market, one of North America's largest open-air markets. Spend the morning sampling Quebec artisan cheeses, fresh maple products, local fruits, charcuterie, and seasonal produce. Chat with vendors and pick up snacks for later in the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Mile End Foodie Neighbourhood Crawl: Walk or take a short bus ride to the Mile End neighbourhood. Hop between iconic spots — grab a smoked meat sandwich at Schwartz's Deli, sample freshly baked bagels at St-Viateur Bagel, and browse quirky boutiques and street art along Boulevard Saint-Laurent and Avenue Fairmount.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Quartier des Spectacles for another evening at the Montreal Jazz Festival. Tonight, consider purchasing a ticket for an indoor ticketed show for a more intimate concert experience with a renowned jazz artist.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the hotel or grab a fresh Montreal-style bagel with cream cheese and lox from a café near Old Montreal (~$8–12 CAD).
meals.lunch: Graze through Jean-Talon Market during the food tour — assemble a market lunch from cheese, charcuterie, fresh bread, and fruit stalls (~$15–20 CAD self-curated).
meals.dinner: Try Damas Restaurant in Mile End or Provisions on Avenue Laurier for a mid-range dinner featuring locally sourced Québécois cuisine with seasonal ingredients (~$40–55 CAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is busiest and most vibrant in the morning — arrive by 9:30–10:00 AM for the best experience. The Mile End is about a 15-minute walk from Jean-Talon, making it easy to combine both in one day. Keep some cash on hand as some market vendors and small Mile End spots may prefer it.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Old Montreal at a leisurely pace — visit the stunning interior of Notre-Dame Basilica (book tickets in advance, ~$15 CAD), then stroll along the Old Port waterfront. Rent a bike along the Lachine Canal path for a scenic morning ride along the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Just for Laughs Festival Street Performances: Head to the Quartier Latin and surrounding streets to catch free outdoor comedy performances, street acts, juggling shows, and colourful parades. The Just for Laughs Festival fills the streets with spontaneous entertainment — wander and stumble upon acts throughout the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Combine both festivals: return to the Quartier des Spectacles for the Jazz Festival evening programming. Enjoy the electric atmosphere as both festivals overlap in this part of the city, with food trucks, street vendors, and multiple stages creating a true Montreal summer celebration.

meals.breakfast: Sit-down breakfast at Crew Collective & Café (housed in a stunning former bank) or L'Gros Luxe near Old Montreal for eggs, fresh pastries, and strong coffee (~$15–20 CAD).
meals.lunch: Grab a casual lunch during the Just for Laughs street festivities — food trucks and local vendors offer everything from tacos to Québécois classics (~$15–20 CAD).
meals.dinner: Dine at Restaurant L'Orignal in Old Montreal, a mid-range spot known for creative charcuterie boards, local meats, and natural wines in a warm, rustic setting (~$40–55 CAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: July 17 falls during peak Just for Laughs season — check the official schedule for any free Gala previews or street show times to plan your afternoon route. The Quartier des Spectacles is walkable from Old Montreal (~20 minutes on foot or 5 minutes by Metro). Book Notre-Dame Basilica tickets online in advance to avoid queues.

day_by_day.morning: Climb up to Mont Royal Park for a morning hike to the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout for panoramic views of the city skyline. Rent a paddle boat on Lac aux Castors or simply relax on the grass and soak in the warm summer weather. Locals gather here on weekends — it's the true heartbeat of Montreal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Plateau-Mont-Royal neighbourhood for a final afternoon of leisurely exploration. Browse the vibrant stretch of Avenue du Mont-Royal — independent boutiques, vintage shops, and local cafés. Pick up edible souvenirs like maple butter, local hot sauce, or Quebec chocolates to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening farewell dinner in Old Montreal, followed by a last stroll along the illuminated waterfront of the Old Port. If the Jazz Festival is still running, end the trip with one final free outdoor concert under the summer sky.

meals.breakfast: Fuel up before the hike at Olive & Gourmando in Old Montreal — beloved for their hearty sandwiches, homemade granola, and excellent coffee (~$15–20 CAD).
meals.lunch: Enjoy a casual lunch on the Plateau at Café Sardine or Comptoir 21 — neighbourhood spots with fresh, creative menus and relaxed vibes (~$20–30 CAD).
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly for the farewell meal at Maison Boulud in the Ritz-Carlton (upscale mid-range, ~$60–80 CAD per person) or keep it local and festive with a rooftop patio dinner at Terrasse Place d'Armes in Old Montreal (~$45–60 CAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Mont Royal is best reached by bus (80 or 11) from downtown or a 30-minute walk from the Plateau. Wear sunscreen and bring water as the summit can be warm in July. Saturday markets and street life on the Plateau are especially lively — leave extra time to wander. Confirm any early checkout requirements with the hotel if departing the following morning.

meals.lunch: Grab artisan bites during the Old Montreal Street Food Walk — think fresh-baked bagels, Quebec cheese curds, and house-made poutine from celebrated local stops along the route.
meals.dinner: Toqué! — Montreal's legendary flagship of Québécois haute cuisine. Chef Bernard Cassini's tasting menu showcases hyper-local, seasonal ingredients with impeccable wine pairings. Reservation essential. Located steps from Old Montreal.

Sample generously and pick up premium provisions to take home.

Begin with a legendary smoked meat sandwich at Schwartz's Deli, then hop to St-Viateur Bagel for wood-fired bagels fresh from the oven, followed by a stop at a craft coffee roaster and a local chocolatier. Stroll through vibrant street art and indie boutiques between tastings.

Tonight, opt for a premium reserved-seat concert at Salle Wilfrid-Pelletier or Maison Symphonique for an elevated indoor performance experience, followed by a nightcap at a rooftop bar overlooking the festival grounds.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at your Old Montreal boutique property — expect a curated spread of local pastries, Quebec yogurt, seasonal fruit, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Grazing lunch throughout the Jean-Talon Market and Mile End Crawl — smoked meat, artisan bagels, imported and local cheeses, maple taffy, and fresh-pressed juice from market vendors.
meals.dinner: Le Mousso — a celebrated avant-garde tasting menu restaurant helmed by Chef Antonin Monat. Inventive, boundary-pushing Québécois cuisine with an exceptional natural wine list. One of Montreal's most talked-about fine dining destinations.

The afternoon atmosphere is lively, family-friendly, and quintessentially Montreal.

A perfect blend of world-class entertainment and Montreal's festival spirit.

meals.breakfast: Olive + Gourmando (Old Montreal) — a beloved brunch institution known for its house-baked sourdough, ricotta toasts, slow-roasted sandwiches, and exceptional coffee. Arrive early or expect a short queue.
meals.lunch: Jun I — an intimate, critically acclaimed Japanese-Québécois fusion restaurant in the downtown core. Chef Jun Tanaka's omakase-style lunch blends pristine Japanese technique with local Quebec ingredients. Perfect pre-festival afternoon fuel.
meals.dinner: Maison Boulud (Ritz-Carlton Montreal) — Chef Daniel Boulud's Montreal outpost offers refined French-inspired cuisine in one of the city's most glamorous dining rooms. The summer terrace is ideal for a warm July evening. Exceptional wine cellar and impeccable service.

day_by_day.notes: The Just for Laughs street performances are free and family-friendly — no tickets required for outdoor shows. Wear sunscreen for the afternoon outdoor festival. Book the Gala show tickets well in advance as premium seats sell out quickly.

day_by_day.afternoon: Montreal Jazz Festival Final Afternoon Session: Spend your last afternoon at the Jazz Festival's free outdoor stages in the Quartier des Spectacles. day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner before departure preparations — a memorable final meal to close out a spectacular Montreal experience.

meals.breakfast: Crew Collective & Café or in-hotel breakfast — indulge in a leisurely final morning spread with Quebec pastries, smoked salmon, local cheeses, and artisan coffee.
meals.lunch: Garde Manger (Old Montreal) — Chef Chuck Hughes' celebrated seafood-forward bistro in a stunning stone-walled Old Montreal setting. Known for its indulgent lobster poutine, fresh oysters, and convivial atmosphere. A Montreal icon.
meals.dinner: Pastel (Mile End) — a critically lauded, intimate fine dining experience offering a creative seasonal tasting menu with Quebec-forward ingredients and a thoughtfully curated natural wine list. A stunning final culinary memory of Montreal.
